decisions.decision: Spec authoring becomes a shared, repo-agnostic skill (deliverable D5), generalized from the GridMarket spec kit (template, build, lint, diagram tooling) and installed like the other shared skills; nothing GridMarket-specific. D1 product spec is written with that skill after integrated approval. Supersedes SD-013 (copy GridMarket kit).
decisions.source: Owner: 'Gridmarket spec kit shouldn't be gridmarket specific and needed to be a shared skill on how to create specs'

decisions.decision: Restructure: Phase 1 = D5 shared spec-authoring skill, D4 shared CI/CD skill extensions + harness hooks, then D1 product specification with a real requirements register (Requirements Engineer) and SysML v2 models (Systems Modeler: structure, interfaces, states, data); owner reviews the spec. Phase 2 = implementation planning derived from the approved spec; full-detail GitHub milestones (D3) created only after the Phase 2 plan is approved. The 54-slice implementation plan at f885e48 is not approved.
decisions.source: Owner at integrated review: 'shouldn't the milestone should have been creating after planning again? ... we actually write the spec first then we can actually plan implementation. Like do we even have models and requirements?'; owner chose 'D4 in Phase 1'

decisions.decision: Visual-review screenshots are committed under top-level evidence/visual/ (not docs/); no account or customer data in captures. Resolves OD-AFC-11.
decisions.source: Owner: 'screen shots isn't docs'; chose 'evidence/visual/ (committed)'

decisions.decision: Align developer-feedback deliverables with the verified Devpost rules (evidence/devpost-feedback-rules.md): per-tool product feedback must include onboarding (zero to hello world) and would-build-again yes/no with reason; AWS Builder services described in product feedback; add optional Feature Requests (description, why it matters, priority Critical/Important/Nice-to-have); friction log entries use the rules' exact fields and are a 10% Stage 1 bonus input. Scribe captures these from Phase 1 on.
decisions.source: Owner: 'Ok lets do it' after rules review

decisions.decision: Owner approved the Phase 1 package at the integrated review (candidate 173e005, manifest digest 4128aa9cdacd1fca06edfb68652258730db107eb6213f6dca3faf9e9cca55e84) with every presented recommendation: OD-AFC-01=A extensions only; OD-AFC-06 track specialist logs via .gitignore negation after scrub; OD-AFC-07 reciprocal non-trigger in use-requirements-system; OD-AFC-08 one spec-authoring skill; OD-AFC-09 vendor spec tools into tools/spec/; OD-AFC-10 REFUSED_NO_VNV is a non-pass row, not a merge block; OA-AFC-A2=A tech-writing lane; OA-AFC-A3=A per-PR review at each integration step; OD-AFC-12 .sdoc register on the local Requirements System host. Continuation granted for Phase 1 under AUTH-AFC-2026-10-11-002 with its exclusions.
decisions.source: Owner: 'Approved'

decisions.decision: Shared-skill validation follows Alphazedehq's stock practice (skills/release-process/tests/test_release_process.py): keep required HQ frontmatter (type, title, okf_status, tags); a per-skill unit test asserts <60 lines and the word limit and required fields; the generic skill-creator quick_validate.py runs only on a temp copy holding the portable fields; BRAN bran-strict validates the full document; trigger checks use a recorded trigger-requests.json + classification results fixture, not a live 1-turn harness run.
decisions.source: Owner: 'Follow what we have been doing in AZHQ stock' (after S01/S02/S03 validator conflict)

decisions.decision: spec-authoring sections read like a real specification: no printed BLUF or Who/What/Why/How/When/Where labels. The opening sentence states the section's point. An unprinted writer's checklist guides each section: Decision (what it decides/defines), Concern (driving requirement/stakeholder concern, cite UIDs), Mechanism (how it works: interfaces, dependencies), Rationale (why this option, alternatives rejected), Verification (how it is proven). Fix the shared skill (rule, template, lint, tests), then rewrite the AFC spec. Inherited from the GridMarket kit; GridMarket's own spec is not changed by this Lifecycle.
decisions.source: Owner at ST-5 spec review: 'the 5 qs are wrong and the bluf all both should not be explicit it should read like a real spec'; chose 'Yes, use those 5'
